# Pandamonium v1.0.61

This train consolidates the Wave 2 and Wave 3 batch: the guided setup wizard is now complete (optional steps plus empty-state routing), node connectivity gains first-class SSH connections, governed agent SSH, and read-only Nextcloud files, model reliability gains zero-content diagnosis and recovery, voice greetings follow the configured identity instead of a legacy deterministic phrase, provider behavior is audited and redacted, memory governance is validated, and the first unscripted tool-use benchmark harness is versioned. Every included issue was merged through a reviewed PR, and the installed acceptance path remains the signed updater with rollback to v1.0.60.

## MAD-785 — Benchmarks: certify unscripted tool use across local and flagship models

### Problem

Prior tests told the model how to answer, so they did not prove autonomous capability discovery or tool use. There was no repeatable, unscripted acceptance set that could be run against both local and flagship models and compared.

### Implementation

Adds `benchmarks/` suite v1: ten categories and sixteen scenarios covering capability discovery, files, books/RAG, calendar, integrations, ORACLE read/control, safe mutation, gated mutation, failure recovery, and long-response completion. Prompts state user goals and constraints without naming the tool, response format, or hidden expected steps. `scripts/run_benchmark.py` captures the selected model, advertised/effective context, prompt/output tokens, latency, tool calls, evidence, and failure reason per run. `docs/benchmarks/ct103-acceptance.md` documents the separate CT103 acceptance procedure. Commit `25433a33`; PR #195.

### Product value and UI visibility

No UI surface. The operator gains a repeatable scorecard to certify agent capability across local and flagship models without scripted hints, and a failed or unavailable tool can never be reported as success.

### Verification

Fixture run 16/16 local and 16/16 flagship with zero false successes. External services are mocked for offline runs; the harness is additive and does not touch runtime paths. PR #195 CI green.

### Configuration, compatibility, and limitations

No dependency, runtime, API, or database change. No local model was configured during CI verification, so live local-model runs remain an operator-side benchmark; CT103 acceptance is documented separately in the harness docs.

### References

## MAD-786 — Memory: validate governed retrieval, extraction, evaluation, and promotion

### Problem

The user needs to know that Pandamonium is remembering usefully, learning safely, and improving rather than accumulating uncontrolled prompt text. Recall relevance, confidence handling, and audit safety needed validation and hardening.

### Implementation

Commit `e3be58c5` governs recall relevance, confidence, and audit safety: false-recall prevention, blocking low-confidence or conflicting facts from silent promotion, and audit-wipe protection. Commit `549bb8c9` adds a deterministic governed-memory acceptance set. The operating model is documented in `docs/memory-governed-learning.md`, defining learning as retrieval and curated memory updates rather than silent weight modification. PR #203.

### Product value and UI visibility

Memory retrieval now reports and respects confidence; low-confidence facts are not silently promoted; users can inspect, correct, disable, export, and delete their memory through the existing surfaces. No new UI.

### Verification

The deterministic acceptance set passes alongside the full regression suite. Larger evaluation gaps — recall quality, latency, and token cost against live data — are listed in the PR body as follow-ups rather than claimed as complete.

### Configuration, compatibility, and limitations

Governance logic and tests only: no dependency, database schema, or data migration. Rollback is reverting `e3be58c5`, which preserves existing memory data and exportability.

### References

## MAD-787 — Providers: audit flagship authentication, discovery, health, and switching

### Problem

Community feedback reported missing OAuth and uncertain flagship-model support. Provider integrations existed, but their public usability — authentication, discovery, health, switching, and capability parity — had to be proven rather than inferred, and two concrete defects sat behind that gap.

### Implementation

Commit `307d1a6b` keeps model attribution immutable when a response is stopped (the stop-backfill path no longer rewrites history). Commit `8cda7399` redacts credentials from provider probe errors so echoed tokens cannot surface in responses or logs. Commit `e59214e7` adds `docs/provider-audit.md`, an audit of supported authentication methods, provider/model discovery, health, switching, and attribution taken from the live code. PR #199.

### Product value and UI visibility

Switching the active model never rewrites historical message attribution. Provider setup failures stay actionable and never expose tokens. Local and remote providers continue to share the canonical model record, and capabilities are advertised only when actually available.

### Verification

Focused auth/discovery tests plus the full regression gate pass; no secrets appear in responses or logs; documentation is derived from live code paths, not aspiration. PR #199 CI green.

### Configuration, compatibility, and limitations

Targeted fixes plus documentation: no provider adapter contract changes and no new dependency. Verification uses mocked provider flows; operator-owned credentials remain the only path to live provider testing.

### References

## MAD-860 — Models: diagnose and recover zero-content OpenAI-compatible responses

### Problem

A clean user testing an OpenAI-compatible model saw alternating successful text and repeated "The model returned an empty response" cards. That fallback collapsed endpoint configuration, provider behavior, stream framing, and parsing failures into one generic dead end with no category and no recovery action, and endpoint/model presence was treated as usable before a minimal completion had been validated.

### Implementation

Commit `ccb4b827` classifies probe failures and persists validation state, so configured, discovered, validated, and failed are distinct and saved fields alone never mean ready. Commit `4f4a082d` recovers empty model turns with one bounded, actionable result — replay is only used when it cannot duplicate a tool or external side effect, otherwise the UI offers an explicit retry. Commit `da7e1354` gates model readiness on the safe test and renders a single retry card. Redacted categories cover authentication, URL/HTTP, TLS, timeout, unsupported model, stream framing, parser failure, zero choices, empty deltas, and zero-content completion. Commits `1a49c5b4`, `ccb4b827`, `4f4a082d`, `da7e1354`; PR #191.

### Product value and UI visibility

One failed request produces one chronological actionable result instead of repeated generic cards, and the guidance tells the user whether to validate settings, change model/endpoint mode, retry, or inspect a redacted diagnostic. First-run readiness no longer claims a model is usable before it has answered once.

### Verification

Focused batches of 330, 66, and 51 checks pass; the full Python suite on the integrated head reports 6068 passed, 5 skipped, and 0 failed (with the MAD-861 follow-up `ec76fd8a`). Intermittent empty responses, streaming and non-streaming fixtures, and clean-install fixtures are covered.

### Configuration, compatibility, and limitations

Reuses existing model probes and settings rather than a second provider-health subsystem. Runtime telemetry keeps redacted provider/model/request correlation without credentials, prompts, or private output. Recovery remains bounded to side-effect-safe paths by design.

### References

- [Linear MAD-860](https://linear.app/madpanda3d/issue/MAD-860/models-diagnose-and-recover-zero-content-openai-compatible-responses)
- [Empty-response recovery PR #191](https://github.com/MADPANDA3D/Pandamonium/pull/191)

## MAD-861 — Voice: remove legacy Jarvis greeting from clean-install behavior

### Problem

The Voice route matched casual greetings and returned a deterministic "I'm doing well. What are we working on?" phrase before the selected model ran, making a clean installation look like it shipped with a built-in Jarvis persona and preventing the configured model and identity from answering.

### Implementation

Commit `2ac21ac0` makes the deterministic greeting explicit and identity-aware: greetings follow the configured model/identity path by default, and the low-latency deterministic mode is opt-in (`voice_deterministic_greeting`, default off) and uses the saved display name when enabled. Commit `9c53a0b7` updates voice headers, labels, transcripts, and fallback copy to use the saved installation identity rather than hardcoded Jarvis labels. Follow-up commit `2c2b3d6d` (PR #207) switches voice target-switch events to the safe `_voice_chat_session()` lookup. PR #193 and PR #207.

### Product value and UI visibility

Voice behaves like the rest of the product: the configured model answers greetings under the saved identity, no private name or phrase is required, and the optional deterministic mode is clearly an installation choice rather than hidden behavior.

### Verification

The full Python suite on the integration head reports 6068 passed, 5 skipped, and 0 failed. A clean fixture with a different agent name proves no private name or phrase is required, and the follow-up test pins a raising session manager to keep the order-dependent `KeyError: Session chat-1 not found` failure from regressing.

### Configuration, compatibility, and limitations

No database change: existing saved display names continue to apply, and private installations keep their chosen identity through the existing settings. The deterministic greeting can be re-enabled explicitly but is off by default. The follow-up `ec76fd8a` is a safety fix and should be kept even if the greeting change were reverted.

### References

- [Linear MAD-861](https://linear.app/madpanda3d/issue/MAD-861/voice-remove-legacy-jarvis-greeting-from-clean-install-behavior)
- [Voice greeting PR #193](https://github.com/MADPANDA3D/Pandamonium/pull/193)
- [Voice session guard PR #207](https://github.com/MADPANDA3D/Pandamonium/pull/207)

## MAD-924 — Onboarding 3/3: wizard optional steps — voice, Portal, plugins, gallery, updates

### Problem

The guided setup wizard covered identity and model, but voice, integrations, plugins, gallery, and update status still required leaving onboarding for dense Settings panels, and there was no honest status-only path for non-admins.

### Implementation

Commit `af064e59` shares the voice preview and Portal connect helpers between the wizard and Settings so both paths use the same proven flows. Commit `58f5016a` completes the optional wizard steps: voice readiness with an inline test, inline MAD MCP Portal connect with live connected state, plugin count with an Add Plugins entry and an honest admin-only note for non-admins, gallery discovery and connect entry, an admin update-state summary with no privileged actions, and "What's next" finish links. Every optional lane shows live state or an explicit skip, and skips persist. Commit `b94ccbb6` updates the guide lane-action count for the added step. PR #187.

### Product value and UI visibility

A non-technical admin can complete the optional setup lanes inside the wizard with the same visual language as Settings, and non-admins see managed status instead of dead ends. No raw backend codes appear in any wizard path.

### Verification

Focused Python and browser coverage exercise the voice and Portal steps end to end; the integrated-main Python suite reports 6068 passed, 5 skipped, and 0 failed (with PR #207), and the `ui-polish` browser guard for the guide lane count was updated. The lane rebased over MAD-935 and resolved the shared `settings.js` import conflict. PR #187 CI green.

### Configuration, compatibility, and limitations

Frontend routing plus reuse of existing owners: no new integration providers, no privileged update actions in the wizard, and no backend contract change. The wizard remains additive; rollback is reverting the feature commits.

## MAD-935 — Settings: SSH connections tab with keyless preset-key connections

### Problem

There was no first-class way to configure SSH connections to nodes, and every connection required interactive authorization. The operator asked for a Settings tab where connections are managed and made keyless with preset keys held with permanence.

### Implementation

Adds the Settings → SSH Connections tab: list configured nodes with label, host, user, port, and status; add, edit, remove, and test; per-connection keyless toggle that generates a keypair on Pandamonium and shows the public key for installation on the node (pasting an existing private key is also supported); host-key pinning; and saved connections that reconnect without re-prompting. Secrets stay on the existing secret-handling path, keys never appear in API responses or logs, and status payloads are redacted. Commit `09f61ea6` fails closed when key generation fails on add, and `bb6f512f` adds the gitleaks allowlist for test-only fixture keys. The lane work was checkpointed at `a1456838` across a provider-credit interruption and resumed to completion. PR #189.

### Product value and UI visibility

A new SSH Connections tab in Settings exposes the full connection lifecycle with human, fail-closed states for wrong key, unknown host key, unreachable node, and authentication failure. The user click on Connect/Test is the approval; there is no stacked confirmation. The public key can be installed once and later reconnects need no authorization prompt.

### Verification

23 focused Python checks, 253 regression checks, and 4 browser checks pass, including the browser tab check. Live-node keyless reconnect remains operator acceptance on CT103.

### Configuration, compatibility, and limitations

Prefers the system OpenSSH path with an explicit managed config; no new dependency. Connection records live in owner-scoped storage and keys are removable per connection. Rollback is reverting PR #189.

## MAD-936 — Agent: governed SSH access to configured nodes

### Problem

The operator wanted to ask the assistant to SSH into a saved VPS and fetch something quickly, without transferring work to the server agent. No governed agent capability existed for bounded SSH operations against the configured connections.

### Implementation

Adds `src/agent_tools/ssh_tools.py`: a governed agent capability that runs bounded SSH operations against saved SSH connections from the settings tab — list and read files, and run per-connection `allowed_commands` policy. Every call is audited with connection, command/output bounds, and no secret exposure; output and timeouts are bounded, there is no interactive TTY, and no arbitrary target or command is possible without an explicit saved connection. Commit `a9e54a2c` adds the red-first coverage, `3ab1a1af` the capability, `775a6120` indexes `ssh_node` for retrieval, and `726544f4` adds the gitleaks allowlist for the test fixture key. PR #197.

### Product value and UI visibility

Text and voice can both trigger a node fetch, and the result is cited as a node-scoped source. Unconfigured nodes, disallowed commands, and authentication failures fail closed with honest copy. No new UI: the capability rides the existing agent surfaces.

### Verification

25 focused tests cover the allowlist, bounds, audit, and denied paths; the full suite reported 5903 checks green at merge. One live smoke against a configured node remains operator acceptance on CT103.

### Configuration, compatibility, and limitations

Depends on the SSH connections tab slice; the `allowed_commands` policy is additive per connection. No new dependency, and shell/authority gates are unchanged. Rollback is reverting `440a7045`.

### References

## MAD-937 — Nextcloud: discover, connect, and browse files read-only over tailnet

### Problem

The operator asked for a Nextcloud integration built like the existing Immich integration, with node-scoped file access over the tailnet: connect an instance, browse real folders, and let the agent answer from files with exact citations.

### Implementation

Adds read-only Nextcloud v1: `src/nextcloud_gallery.py` reuses the Immich connection/status/cache patterns and the gallery source model; `routes/nextcloud_routes.py` exposes connect/test/status plus bounded browse, search, and read; `src/agent_tools/nextcloud_tools.py` registers the agent capability with node-scoped citations (node + path). Connection uses the Nextcloud app-password flow with a tailnet discovery probe (`status.php`/WebDAV) in the Add Tailscale flow. Content is registered as a node-scoped file source; secrets and redacted paths are excluded per the existing gallery-source patterns; there is no write or upload in v1. Commit `a6f76208` adds red-first coverage, `d18e2529` the feature, and `b44eb02b` indexes `nextcloud_files` for retrieval. PR #201.

### Product value and UI visibility

Settings → Integrations gains Nextcloud connection and status alongside the existing gallery sources, and the agent answers questions from Nextcloud files with an exact citation. Unreachable and auth-failure states render honest errors with no secrets in responses.

### Verification

Focused tests and a browser check pass; committed fixtures contain no private hostnames. Live-instance acceptance — connect cloud.pandamonium.ai or a tailnet node, browse a real folder, and read a file through the API with an exact-citation agent answer — remains operator-side on CT103.

### Configuration, compatibility, and limitations

Read-only v1 by design: no dependency additions, no write/upload, and bounded size/timeouts on all reads. Rollback is reverting `d18e2529`; connection records remain in owner-scoped storage.
